brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Getting Started with ESource Bookkeeping Tool

questions.question: What is the web address you use to sign in to the ESource Bookkeeping Tool?
choices: The address your owner gave you
www.esourcebookkeeping.com
Your firm's email domain
The address is sent to you via email
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—your owner provides your firm's specific web address, which you should bookmark for easy access.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool is customized for your firm, so you won't use a generic web address. Your owner will give you the specific address to use.

questions.question: What happens if a computer goes 14 days without connecting to the internet?
choices: You must add the client again
The books lock for safety until you sign in with a new code
Your backup files are deleted
Your staff member's email is removed from the License tab
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the tool locks the books as a security measure if a computer hasn't checked in for 14 days.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool has a built-in safety feature that prevents unauthorized access. After 14 days offline, you'll need to sign in again with a fresh code to unlock the books.

questions.question: Which three things make this bookkeeping tool different from others?
choices: It is free, cloud-based, and works offline
It carries your brand, your data stays with you, and everything is locked to your firm
It automatically files taxes, integrates with all banks, and requires no backups
It allows unlimited staff, stores data in the cloud, and provides tax advice
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—those three core features protect your firm's brand, data privacy, and security.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool is designed around three key principles: branding your firm, keeping data local on your computers, and encrypting everything so only approved people can access it.

questions.question: What file formats can you upload for banks other than Wells Fargo?
choices: Only PDF files
CSV, Quicken (QFX), QuickBooks (QBO), or OFX
Excel spreadsheets only
Only OFX and CSV files
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—most banks let you download in one of these four formats, with Quicken and QuickBooks files being ideal because they include account numbers and balances.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Different banks support different download formats. The tool accepts CSV, Quicken, QuickBooks, and OFX files from most banks to give you flexibility.

questions.question: When should you download a backup of your books?
choices: Once a month
Only when you add a new client
At the end of every work session
Once a year at tax time
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—consistent backups at the end of each session protect your firm's data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Since your books live on your computer rather than in the cloud, backing up regularly is critical. Make it a habit to download a backup every time you finish working.

questions.question: What is the 3-2-1 backup rule described in this course?
choices: Keep 3 monthly backups, 2 yearly backups, and 1 quarterly backup
Keep 3 copies on 2 kinds of storage, with 1 away from the office
Keep 3 backups on a thumb drive, 2 on your computer, and 1 in email
Keep 3 copies encrypted, 2 copies unencrypted, and 1 in the cloud
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—this strategy ensures you have redundant copies across different media and locations for maximum protection.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The 3-2-1 rule is a data protection standard: three copies, on at least two different types of storage media, with at least one copy stored away from your office.

questions.question: Why are bank and book statements never uploaded to ESource's servers?
choices: It would slow down the tool's performance
Because your data stays with you and lives only on your firm's own computers
Because the company runs out of server space
Because clients prefer to manage their own data online
questions.feedback_correct: Right—this is a core design principle that gives your firm complete control and privacy over sensitive financial data.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool is built so that sensitive financial data never leaves your office. This keeps your firm's data and your clients' information under your complete control.

questions.question: If an owner wants to add a staff member, what must they do first?
choices: Send the staff member a link to download the tool
Create a username and password for the staff member
Add the staff member with their own work email on the License tab
Have the staff member sign in and set up their own profile
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the owner must add each staff member individually with their own work email so they sign in as themselves.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The owner controls access through the License tab. Each person needs their own work email so they sign in individually and the system can track who accessed what.

questions.question: When sorting transactions, what should you do if you mark "Remember" when picking a category?
choices: The transaction will be sent to the tax preparer automatically
A rule is created so lines like that sort themselves next month
The category is saved only for that client
You must re-enter the category every time you see a similar line
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—leaving "Remember" checked builds rules that automate sorting over time, so you answer fewer questions each month.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The "Remember" feature is a learning tool. When you check it, the tool creates a rule, so similar transactions automatically sort themselves in the future and reduce your workload.

questions.question: What should you do before sending an Excel report package to a client or their tax preparer?
choices: Encrypt the file with a password
Ask the client to sign a confidentiality agreement
Review the reports first, as these are tools for trained professionals, not tax advice
Get approval from ESource AI Group
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—professional review is essential before sharing reports because the tool provides data organization, not tax advice.
questions.feedback_incorrect: These reports are powerful tools for bookkeeping professionals, but they don't include tax advice. It's your responsibility to review the reports before sending them to ensure accuracy and appropriateness.
